question: what does the delta-h map look like in a spine-anchored frame, knowing it carries the frame artifact
not_a_validated_effect: this map is Eulerian by construction. The expert landmarks measured tissue displacement of 11.3-30.2 mm median with an axial fraction of 0.24-0.89, and the measured spatial gradient of h is 0.09-0.12 mm/mm median with p90 0.29, so this map contains a frame artifact estimated at 1.4 mm typical and up to 12 mm in steep zones. It is the comparison arm for the rib frame, not the deliverable

measurand.name: soft_tissue_mm
measurand.definition: fat_mm + muscle_mm + other_mm along the lung-to-skin path
measurand.reason: D-044 merged fat and muscle into one tissue

frame.shared_grid: DIR-Lab COPDgene phases are loaded onto one identical grid, so absolute coordinates are directly comparable and no rigid alignment is applied
frame.radial_origin: per-slice centroid of the fixed-phase filled body mask, reused unchanged for both phases
frame.axial_coordinate: z of the skin point normalised to the fixed-phase vertebral column extent
frame.reason: one single frame is applied to both phases; that is what makes the comparison Eulerian, and using the spine rather than the lung avoids normalising to a landmark that breathing itself moves

occupancy.bins_reported: only bins that clear the minimum in BOTH phases
occupancy.reason: a delta needs both sides; a bin resolved in one phase only is not a delta

per_bin_uncertainty.method: bootstrap standard error of each phase median, combined in quadrature

reporting_rule.resolved_bin: absolute delta-h exceeds twice its combined bootstrap uncertainty
reporting_rule.reason: bins that do not clear their own uncertainty carry no zone information and are shown as unresolved rather than coloured

out_of_scope: calling this a validated respiratory effect
using it to choose electrode placement before the rib frame confirms or refutes it
